text: An agent-step entry carries the decision code of the step from LOV-DECISION in force, a rule ID with its rule version, the agent version of the legacy form <agent>@<policy>/<prompt>, the model version the run names, the inputs reference of the masked snapshot, the recommendation with its confidence in L1 and null in SHADOW, the applied rule result as final_call, and actions holding the agent run id, the mode, fallback and the reason TIMED_OUT, SCHEMA or NO_POLICY; a step with no policy or prompt in force holds no agent version.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives the columns and no source names the code of an agent step or the placement of the run id, the mode and the fallback, and the record must still be assertable and groupable.
read: RWB-TE-013 sections 4, 7, 8 and 12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-003, -009, -012, -014 and -031 and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.3.4.3.
confirm: Solution architect with the P7 business analyst and the reference-data owner
impact: Medium: the placement is a contract choice made once and the codes become reference rows, so a new code is a data change and no scenario changes.

text: MSG-P7-009 carries every schema refusal of this slice - a decision code outside LOV-DECISION, a rule ID without its rule version, an agent version outside the contract form, a missing inputs reference or decided time - naming the field, and it keeps the legacy field names character for character; the 404 answer and the chain-break report keep a placeholder for id and text.
why: The FSD names MSG-P7-009 without a text and allocates no id to the other two outcomes, and the field names are already asserted by the decision-log store slice.
confirm: Business analyst, P7, with the message and localisation owners
impact: Low: no behaviour changes; only the wording and the ids of three outcomes are deferred.

text: The seven platform contract stories the patterns add and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are wave 0 or contract fakes, the authorise answer of rwb-access arrives through the platform guard the reads declare, and the entry is validated against the published RWB-P10-TE013-CON contract row and its fake until that contract lands; the metadata rows stay as the Work Package fixes them and the story stays Day 1.
why: The story line fixes the build dependency as empty and the contract dependency as RWB-P10-TE013-CON alone, the patterns add H rows that are not in it, and no authorise path exists in the Ownership Map.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5 and R5.7; P7 context pack; Ownership Map v1 P4 rows.
impact: Low: no work moves; the dependency bookkeeping differs from the metadata row and is visible in one place.

text: The per-service login is referred to as 'the rwb-decision login (DP-02)' with no name, the consumer group, the Flyway user, the environment names and the property names come from the service template, and the nightly chain check that covers these entries keeps the owner, the time and the overlap policy of the decision-log store slice.
why: No source names the login or the Schedule parameters, and this story must not invent a credential or a time of day.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-02 and DP-10; P7 context pack; FSD P7 v3 AC-BG-P7-001-01; RWB-TE-013 section 13.
confirm: Solution architect with the platform DB and workflow platform owners
impact: Low: configuration only, settled once in the service template.

text: The model version of an agent step is copied from the run the rwb-agent contract reports and is never a literal in this service, so the tests assert equality between the entry and the run fixture.
why: The legacy story records the model version as the value the run names and no source names the model version of agent INTAKE.
read: RWB-TE-013 sections 4, 11 and 12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 DF-DEC-006.
impact: Low: the assertion is an equality and not a literal, so a model change needs no story change.

text: The decision-record library of DP-03 appends the record in the calling service's own schema inside the step's transaction and publishes rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 from its outbox, and this service collects it into the ledger; the legacy sentence that the client publishes no event is superseded, because the central ledger cannot exist otherwise.
why: The legacy story describes the monolith writer, and DP-03 and the architecture outrank the story master in the source precedence.
read: RWB-TE-013 section 12 and section 4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03 and R3; TSD P7 v2 T5.3.
impact: Medium: the record path is one local commit plus one event instead of one distributed write, which is the point of the split.

text: The artefact of the superseded Work Package B-P7-05 that stood at the fixed story path is replaced in full by this Work Package, its substance is carried forward, and every CG and ASM citation in the new file resolves to a row written here; a v2 copy is not made because it would be a path outside the Write only block.
why: Root rule 1 forbids editing an existing file while the Work Package fixes this exact path as the deliverable, and the earlier artefact cited rows that no register holds.
read: status.json entry B-P7-05; the file at the fixed path before this Work Package; the Write only block of WP B2-P7-007.
applied_in: Sections 1 and 6 and the edit log
impact: Low: one file at a fixed path, with no citation left dangling.

text: The agent fallback rate is counted from the ledger by agent version and month, its threshold stays below 10 percent per month, and the measure definition and the published operation belong to rwb-reporting; this service only makes the count readable.
why: The legacy story sets the threshold and names no owner of the definition, and the data lake is removed, so reporting reads events.
read: RWB-TE-013 section 2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.1 and A2.1.4.3; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17.
confirm: Business analyst, P7, with the reporting owner
impact: Low: the stored fact is complete, and only the measure name and the period grain are deferred.

text: The record event is published and consumed under the name rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1, and its EV number is left open until the event catalog ties it to one of the three P7 event rows.
why: The context pack lists three P7 events without names and the TSD names the event without a number.
read: P7 context pack Events; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; Ownership Map v1.
impact: Low: the topic, the name and the payload do not change; only the catalog row is deferred.
